newsitem.title: UK: Shipbuilding to remain in excess of demand - report.
newsitem.headline: Shipbuilding to remain in excess of demand - report.

text.p: World shipbuilding will continue to provide tonnage surplus to requirements between 1998 and 2000, according to a report by a Japanese industry association.

The Association for Structural Improvement of the Shipbuilding Industry (ASIS) said, "The yearly average of shipbuilding tonnage from 1998 to 2000 will be 34.5 million deadweight tonnes for both tankers and bulk carriers.
"If shipbuilding continues at such a level, market conditions will not be greatly improved."

ASIS forecast combined yearly demand for tankers and bulk carriers during the period to be 27.2 million dwt. It added that the demand figure corresponded to 93 percent of total ship completions in 1996.
Its latest report on world shipbuilding demand forecasts said it assumed that excess tonnage of tankers and bulk carriers would remain at an average three percent during the period.
The association predicted that increases in oil production in non-OPEC areas would slow down after 1998, although it also said production would be maintained in some areas including the North Sea.
It added, "Iraqi oil exports via the Dortyol pipeline are predicted to gradually increase. These factors will reduce tanker demand growth."
However, ASIS said demand for tanker tonnage would increase by the end of 2000 "due to a replacement demand for those built in the mid-1970s, which will be scrapped."
